paragraphs: On Thursday at lunch break, Lily and Mia played with a ball on the school field. Mia ran after the ball, and her foot hit a stone. She fell on the grass and hit her knee. There was blood on her knee, and she sat very still. Lily ran to her, because nobody else was near them. "Are you OK?" asked Lily. "It was an accident," said Mia. "I did not see the stone."

Lily helped Mia walk slowly to the nurse's room. Nurse Jill looked at Mia's knee and then at her face. "Sit here, Mia, and tell me what happened," she said. "I fell on the field, and I hit my knee on a stone," said Mia. "Lily saw it." "That is right," said Lily. "Mia did not hit her head, and she got up by herself."

"Let me check your knee," said Nurse Jill. She washed it with clean water and looked at it carefully. "Where is the pain?" she asked. "Only in my knee," said Mia. "Is it a sharp pain, or a slow pain?" asked Nurse Jill. "It is a sharp pain at first, and then it goes away," said Mia. "It is sore when I move my leg." "Does it bother you when you walk?" asked Nurse Jill. "A little," said Mia. "My head is fine, and my arms are fine." "Can you move your foot?" asked Nurse Jill. Mia moved her foot up and down, and she did not make a sound. "Do you feel tired or hot?" asked Nurse Jill. "No, I feel fine," said Mia.

"It is only a small cut," said Nurse Jill. "You are fit and strong, so your knee will be better in a few days." She put a bandage on Mia's knee. "Now I have some advice," she said. "Do not run today, and keep the bandage dry." "Your knee may be sore tomorrow, so walk slowly." "May I play football on Saturday?" asked Mia. "Come and see me on Friday," said Nurse Jill. "I will look at your knee again."

Afterwards, Nurse Jill wrote a note for Mia's mom. "Give this note to your mom tonight," she said. "It says what happened." Lily picked up Mia's bag. "Shall I carry it for you?" she asked. "Yes, please," said Mia. "Thank you for helping me." "That is what friends do," said Lily, and they walked to the library together.
